prompt.context: The beverage department of a regional supermarket has seen a drop in revenue over the last year and has hired your firm to determine the cause of the decline and recommend ways to reverse the trend.
prompt.question: What is causing the decline in beverage revenue, and what recommendations would you make to reverse the trend?

clarifying_info.q: What region does the client operate in?
clarifying_info.a: The client is a leading regional grocer within the southeastern U.S.
The competitive landscape has not changed in the last year.

clarifying_info.q: Is the revenue decline across the entire store or specific to beverages?
clarifying_info.a: The revenue decline is specifically within the beverage segment.
The client wants to find the cause of the declining revenue and recommendations for how to stop the decline.

exhibits.title: Revenues and Costs by Beverage Category
exhibits.shows: A table breaking down beverage sales by category (Sodas, Waters, Others) for 2014 and 2015, showing gallons sold (MM), price per gallon ($), and cost per gallon ($) — all figures are averages per store.

exhibits.title: Sodas by Brand
exhibits.shows: A table breaking down soda sales into three brands (Brand A, Brand B, Value Brand) for 2014 and 2015, showing gallons sold (MM) and revenue ($M) — all figures are averages per store.

framework: Focus on revenue and its levers: price and quantity (volume) — avoid costs unless prompted
Segment beverage revenue by category to isolate where the decline is occurring
For the declining category, further segment by brand/SKU to pinpoint the root cause
Identify price changes at the brand level (revenue ÷ volume) to determine pricing dynamics
Develop recommendations using 4P's (Price, Promotion, Product, Placement) to reverse the decline

questions.prompt: Calculate total beverage revenue in 2014 and 2015 for each category, and identify which category is driving the overall decline.
questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply gallons by price/gallon for each category and year, compare year-over-year, and identify that only Sodas declined while Waters and Others grew slightly.

steps: Total change: -$6M + $0.3M + $1M = -$4.7M net decline, driven entirely by Sodas
math.answer: Sodas are the only category with declining revenue (-$6M), more than offsetting modest gains in Waters (+$0.3M) and Others (+$1M).

questions.prompt: Within Sodas, calculate per-unit prices for each brand in 2014 and 2015, and identify what is driving the soda revenue decline.
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute implied price = Revenue / Gallons for each brand. Brand A and Brand B prices are stable at $1/gallon; Value Brand price dropped sharply from $0.60 to $0.40 while its volume more than doubled. The revenue loss in Brand A (-$20M) is the immediate driver, but the dramatic volume shift from Brand A to Value Brand (at a much lower price) is the structural cause.

steps: Value Brand is cannibalizing Brand A volume at a price 60% lower, collapsing blended average price from $0.90 to $0.70/gal
math.answer: The Value Brand's price dropped from $0.60 to $0.40/gallon while volume surged from 25MM to 60MM gallons, cannibalizing Brand A. Despite more total gallons sold, the lower blended price caused a $6M soda revenue decline.

brainstorming.prompt: The client would like to hear your recommendations for how to reverse the decline in revenue of the beverage segment.

categories.name: Price
ideas: Raise the Value Brand price back toward $0.50–$0.60/gal to recover margin without losing all volume gains
Test price elasticity of Value Brand with a phased price increase
Introduce tiered pricing or multi-pack promotions for Brand A to defend its volume

categories.name: Promotion
ideas: Run targeted promotions for Brand A to recover lost customers
Promote brand story / quality differentiation of Brand A vs. Value Brand
Use loyalty-program data to identify Value Brand switchers and target them with Brand A offers

categories.name: Product
ideas: Introduce new SKUs or flavors for Brand A to reinvigorate interest
Reposition Value Brand as a distinct sub-category (e.g., house brand) with different packaging to reduce direct comparison
Bundle beverages with complementary products to drive basket size

categories.name: Placement
ideas: Move Value Brand to a less premium shelf position to reduce impulse comparison with Brand A
Co-locate Brand A with complementary snacks to drive cross-category sales
Ensure Brand A has prominent end-cap or eye-level placement

recommendation: The primary cause of the beverage revenue decline is the Value Brand's steep price cut (from $0.60 to $0.40/gal), which attracted volume away from Brand A and collapsed the blended soda price per gallon
Recommend adjusting the Value Brand's price upward to reduce cannibalization of Brand A and improve blended revenue per gallon
Additionally, improve differentiation between Brand A and the Value Brand through packaging, shelf placement, and targeted promotions
risks: Raising Value Brand price may alienate value-oriented customers who switched to it, potentially reducing total soda volume
Any attempt to adjust Brand A or Brand B pricing could strain supplier relationships
If differentiation efforts are insufficient, volume may simply shift between brands without revenue recovery
next_steps: Explore optimal pricing strategy for Value Brand through price elasticity analysis or A/B pricing tests
Explore bundling and cross-promotion opportunities to increase Brand A sales
Explore marketing and packaging changes to strengthen Brand A's perceived differentiation from Value Brand
Explore shelf placement options to reduce direct price comparison between Value Brand and Brand A/B
